title: ci(docs): build the docs site on a free GitHub runner every 6 hours and deploy it prebuilt; turn Vercel's Git deployments off
body:
## Why

The Vercel team `object-stack` is billed ~$125 per cycle, and 97% of that is **Build CPU Minutes**. This repository's docs project (`objectstack`, Root Directory `apps/docs`) costs ~$70 a month of it. Measured on 2026-10-12:

- **~533 deployments a day are Git-integration PREVIEW deployments** for `claude/*`, `gh-readonly-queue/*`, `board-archive*` and `changeset-release/*` branches. Each one clones the monorepo, runs `scripts/vercel-ignore-docs.sh` for ~25 s and is canceled, and is **still billed**: billed CPU-minutes divided by production-build wall-minutes is 12–15, more than the 8-vCPU build machine can produce alone, so the canceled ones are in the bill. That is ~40% of the project's cost.
- **~34 production builds a day** come from pushes to `main` (which gets ~87 commits a day).

The maintainer's ruling, verbatim:

> 文档站应该只有主分支需要部署，而且应该用免费的

This repository is public, so standard GitHub-hosted runners (`ubuntu-latest`) are free. The docs are now built there and uploaded to Vercel already built, so **Vercel bills zero build minutes** for this project.

## What changes

**`apps/docs/vercel.json`**
- Adds `"git": { "deploymentEnabled": false }` (the boolean form in https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json). No branch push creates a Vercel deployment any more, so nothing is cloned, canceled or billed.
- Removes `ignoreCommand`, which only ever ran inside a Git deployment. `scripts/vercel-ignore-docs.sh` and its self-test (which no workflow ran) are deleted with it. The failure-direction rule that script's header spelled out, that a wrong skip silently stops publishing, now lives in the new workflow's header and is enforced there.
- `buildCommand` / `installCommand` are unchanged: `vercel build` runs them, and ci.yml's **Build Docs** gate still reads `buildCommand` from this file and runs it on every docs PR.

**`.github/workflows/docs-deploy.yml`** (new)
- **Triggers:** `schedule` every six hours at `43 0,6,12,18 * * *` UTC, plus `workflow_dispatch`. There is no `push` trigger and no paths list to maintain. The docs refresh **at most six hours** behind `main`, and **"Run workflow" on the workflow's Actions page publishes `main` immediately**. Four builds a day keep this job from competing with CI for runners. The hours stay out of the crowded 01–07 UTC nightly window and the board snapshot's 02/08/14/20; the minute is off the top of the hour. The reasoning is in the file.
- **Runner:** `ubuntu-latest`, `timeout-minutes: 30`. ci.yml's forced Build Docs takes ~4 min on this runner class.
- **Steps:** checkout → Node 22 and pnpm (the repo's own `setup-pnpm` action, and the pnpm store cache key ci.yml uses) → `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` → `vercel pull --yes --environment=production` → `vercel build --prod` → assert `apps/docs/.next/BUILD_ID` and `.vercel/output/config.json` exist → `vercel deploy --prebuilt --prod` → write the deployment URL to the run summary.
- **CLI pinned:** `npx --yes vercel@60.1.3`. Env `VERCEL_ORG_ID=team_06nvlGKZCkwhzdXmRdxeCNnB` and `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID=prj_KbPkuEVCj8viErlaC0wBUgMIYZWe` are identifiers, not secrets. The token comes from `secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN`.
- **Run from the repository root, not `apps/docs`.** In vercel/vercel's CLI source, `vercel build` builds `<cwd>/<rootDirectory>` and writes `<cwd>/.vercel/output`, and `vercel deploy` checks that `<cwd>/<rootDirectory>` exists before uploading `<cwd>/.vercel/output`. Run from `apps/docs`, the project's Root Directory setting would resolve to `apps/docs/apps/docs`. From the root, the build runs vercel.json's commands with `apps/docs` as cwd, which is exactly what Build Docs runs.
- `TURBO_FORCE=true` on the build. A fresh runner has no turbo cache and this job passes no remote-cache credentials, so nothing can be replayed today. Forcing keeps it that way if either changes, for the same reason Build Docs forces.
- **`concurrency: { group: docs-deploy-production, cancel-in-progress: true }`.** Every run builds the tip of `main`, so a canceled run loses nothing a later run doesn't deliver.
- **Failure direction: red, never skipped green.** Each of these fails the run with an `::error::`: a missing `VERCEL_TOKEN`, a `workflow_dispatch` from any ref other than `main` (that would otherwise publish a branch to production), and a build that exits 0 without output.

## Secret: in place

`VERCEL_TOKEN` exists as an **objectstack-ai organization secret** (updated 2026-10-12T03:10:52Z), and `GET /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/organization-secrets` lists it, so this repository can see it. `secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN` resolves an org secret the same way it resolves a repo secret, so the workflow needs no change. Nothing in this PR creates tokens or sets secrets.

## Verification plan, right after merge

The deploy path cannot run before merge: `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` only see the workflow once it is on the default branch, and this job refuses any ref but `main`. So the first real run is the verification:

1. `gh workflow run docs-deploy.yml --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ref main`
2. `gh run watch <run-id> --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`. Every step should go green through **Deploy the prebuilt output to production**. The run summary prints the deployment URL.
3. On Vercel, that deployment should be **READY**, marked Production, with source CLI, and the production domain should serve it.
4. Branches keep being pushed all day. Confirm the `objectstack` project's deployment list shows **no** new Git-triggered deployments after the merge commit. This is the `git.deploymentEnabled: false` half.

If step 2 fails, production keeps serving the last deployment the Git integration made (stale, not down). Fix forward and re-run with "Run workflow". The part not exercised before merge is `vercel build` with the pinned CLI against this Next.js 16.3 app; the build command it runs is the one Build Docs proves on this PR.

## Validation done

- **`git.deploymentEnabled: false` is already observable on this PR.** Vercel reads `vercel.json` from the pushed commit. This PR's head (`91f9eda3f5`) has **zero** commit statuses from Vercel and no GitHub deployments. The sibling PR #22930, branched from the same `main` commit and so still carrying the old `vercel.json`, got the usual `Vercel: pending "Vercel is deploying your app"` (03:35:51Z) followed by `success "Canceled by Ignored Build Step"` (03:36:40Z), which is exactly the billed, canceled preview this PR removes.
- `actionlint` 1.7.12, with shellcheck 0.11.0: clean on `docs-deploy.yml`.
- The repo's workflow-scanning gates were run locally on this branch, all exit 0: `check:node-version`, `check:pnpm-acquisition`, `check:workflow-step-name-quoting`, `check:workflow-status-functions`, `check:required-contexts`, `check:stall-guard-budget`, `check:shard-attestation`, `check:pm-dispatch-gates`, `check:pm-expected-skips`, `check:agent-test-spelling`, `check:pnpm-filter-targets`, plus `check-self-test-wired`, `check-step-collectors`, `check-whole-set-label-write`, `check-aggregator-roster` and `check-ci-filter-parity`. `check-self-test-workflow-commands` reds identically on untouched `main` (a `::group::` line printed by `scripts/ci/select-shard-timings-run.mjs --self-test`), so that red is not from this diff.
- No full docs/monorepo build was run locally. Build Docs on this PR runs the production build command.

## Notes

- Searched for an existing issue or PR on this (`vercel`, `docs deploy`) and found none open. This builds on the closed history of the docs-deploy cost work (#12743 / #12746, which added the ignore command removed here).
- Releases nothing from any published package, so `skip-changeset`.
- Optional hardening for later: move `VERCEL_TOKEN` into a GitHub Environment restricted to `main`. Today any same-repo workflow can read the org secret, like every other secret here.

Clause-②: no
